notes: WHY THIS FILE IS A THOUSAND TIMES SMALLER THAN CRYSTAL'S.
A Gen 1-3 manifest is an ADDRESS BOOK. Those cartridges are flat arrays,
so the importer cannot find anything without being told where it is, and
rom_manifest_crystal.json is 3.7 MB of exactly that.
A Nintendo DS cartridge is a FILESYSTEM. Platinum holds 340 files in 89
directories behind an FNT/FAT pair, and every Gen 4 extraction stage opens
/fielddata/land_data/land_data.narc. There is no address to record, so an
address table here would be invented rather than measured, and inventing
one is worse than not having one.
So this manifest carries what it can honestly carry: which dumps are this
game, and what the cartridge says about itself. src/import/RomExtractorGen4.lua
reads none of it; RomImporter's decodeManifest reads romSha1, and that gate
is the reason the file has to exist at all.
The few Gen 4 numbers that ARE addresses do not belong here either. The
type chart is in overlay 16 and gObjectEventGfxTexturesTable in overlay 5,
and both are found by a STRUCTURAL search rather than by an offset, because
Rev 0 is a different binary and a hard-coded offset would silently read the
wrong bytes out of it. See docs/gen4-platinum.md.

filesystem.note: Counted by walking the FNT/FAT this manifest describes, not assumed.
